name: Boulder Care
one_liner: Telehealth medication treatment for opioid and alcohol use (Suboxone, naltrexone and others) through an app, mainly with Medicaid, in seven states.
best_for: Adults on Medicaid in Oregon, Washington, Ohio, North Carolina, New Mexico or Michigan who want opioid treatment by video
People who want buprenorphine, including long-acting injections, with peer support
People who want naltrexone or acamprosate for drinking
not_for: Anyone in crisis or overdose: call 911, or call or text 988
People who need medically supervised detox or residential treatment
People who want to pay cash in a state where self-pay is not offered
short_description: App-based telehealth treatment for opioid and alcohol use disorder with medication and peer support; Medicaid and commercial insurance in seven states.
long_description: Boulder Care is a US telehealth addiction treatment provider. Through its app you have video visits with clinicians who can prescribe buprenorphine (Suboxone, Zubsolv, Sublocade, Brixadi), naltrexone, acamprosate and other medications, and you can message a care team that includes peer recovery specialists. Boulder says it serves seven states; its eligibility page names Oregon, Washington, Ohio, North Carolina, New Mexico and Michigan. It accepts Medicaid (which covers about three-quarters of its patients) and many commercial plans, varying by state, and offers self-pay only in select states without a published program fee; it says discount programs can bring some medications to about $40 a week. Boulder's employees published a retrospective study of 22,064 patients in JMIR (2026) reporting 71% still in treatment at six months, with no control group. Its privacy policy says third parties may collect data on its site for interest-based advertising.

pricing.starting_price: Copay with Medicaid or insurance; self-pay in select states (price not published)
pricing.notes: About 75% of patients use Medicaid; commercial plans vary by state. Self-pay offered only in some states; Boulder says discount programs can bring some medications to about $40/week. No program fee published.

privacy.notes: Says it does not sell personal data, but allows third parties to collect information on its site for interest-based advertising (NAI opt-out offered); clinical records under its Notice of Privacy Practices.

seo.meta_description: Boulder Care provides virtual Suboxone treatment for opioid addiction with compassionate, judgment-free care from licensed clinicians.

faqs.q: How much does Boulder Care cost?
faqs.a: Boulder Care accepts Medicaid and commercial insurance, often with low or no copays. Self-pay options are available where insurance isn't accepted. Medication costs are separate and may be covered by insurance or assistance programs.

faqs.q: Is Boulder Care effective for opioid addiction?
faqs.a: MAT with buprenorphine is the gold standard for opioid use disorder treatment. Boulder Care follows evidence-based protocols. Their compassionate approach helps patients stay engaged in treatment, which is key to recovery success.

faqs.q: What states does Boulder Care serve?
faqs.a: Boulder Care currently operates in select states with ongoing expansion. Check their website for current availability. State telemedicine regulations affect controlled substance prescribing.

faqs.q: What happens at my first Boulder Care appointment?
faqs.a: Your first appointment includes a medical evaluation, discussion of treatment goals, and if appropriate, a Suboxone prescription. The prescriber assesses your history and creates a personalized treatment plan. Appointments are typically 15-30 minutes via video.

clinical_trials.study: Retention of Boulder Care patients in telehealth-only buprenorphine treatment, 2019–2025

citation.authors: Monico LB, Bambury EA, Foreman JK, Avila M, Martin SA
citation.title: Retention in Telehealth-Delivered Buprenorphine Treatment for Opioid Use Disorder: Multistate Retrospective Cohort Study

clinical_trials.outcome: Retention 86.8% at month 1 and 71.0% at month 6, declining gradually to 24 months; no control group; all authors employed by Boulder Care.

primary_uses: Buprenorphine treatment for opioid use disorder by video
Naltrexone or acamprosate for alcohol use disorder
Peer recovery support through the app

availability.note: Seven states per Boulder; its eligibility page names OR, WA, OH, NC, NM and MI. Does not serve other states.

patient_summary: You download the Boulder Care app, check eligibility, and meet a clinician by video who can prescribe buprenorphine (Suboxone and others) or naltrexone, with a peer recovery specialist and care team you can message. Most patients use Medicaid or commercial insurance; self-pay is offered only in some states. It serves a small number of states, including Oregon, Washington, Ohio, North Carolina, New Mexico and Michigan.
